title: The Most Dangerous Thing Schools Can Produce Is a Child Who No Longer Knows They Are Gifted
author: Kevin Stinehart
summary: Schools inadvertently damage gifted students by creating educational environments where capability and challenge no longer align. When instruction moves too slowly for advanced learners, students begin to doubt their own abilities because effort no longer produces success. This erodes the gifted child's sense of intellectual identity and capability. The result is students who were genuinely gifted but no longer believe themselves to be, whose self-concept has been damaged by years of insufficient challenge. The danger isn't just underachievement—it's the internalization of low expectations that students carry forward. Schools have a responsibility to create appropriately challenging learning experiences for advanced students, not as enrichment add-ons, but as core instructional responsibility.
